newsitem.title: UK: Turkey gives investors delightful spread on bond.
newsitem.headline: Turkey gives investors delightful spread on bond.

text.p: Turkey paid investors generously to raise money on Monday in a bid to launch a successful transaction after a delayed deal.
Turkey's $300 million five-year offering was priced more generously than planned which led to healthy demand and the bond being increased, dealers said.

"Turkey could have priced the deal much more tightly than it did, but wanted a successful transaction so was prepared to pay-up," a co-lead manager said, adding: "Its very cheap and the spread will tighten."
Turkey was targeting a spread in the high 200 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, but the bond was priced to yield 350 b.p. over the 6.625 percent April 2002 U.S. Treasury.

"If Turkey had given any more yield to investors we might have thought it was a dog deal," a banker said, adding: "Turkey does not have a natural dollar investor base so this is not cost-effective funding."
The bond pays a psychologically attractive coupon of 10.0 percent.
"It is a nice coupon which will appeal to retail investors," a dealer said.
Bankers said they had sold their allotted paper to Turkish funds and private banks in Switzerland as well as into Benelux. Other said they sold paper to a mixture of accounts in Europe and the U.S.
Turkey held roadshows in key financial centres in Europe, Asia and the U.S. in April.
Joint lead managers for the transaction were JP Morgan and SBC Warburg.
"It's a good result for Turkey and a big achievement to get a five-year bond," a syndicate manager said.
Dealers said Turkey's mark bonds had tightened significantly due to its large customer base in Germany.
International credit rating agencies recently cut Turkey's debt rating. Turkey is rated B1 by Moody's Investors Service and B by Standard & Poor's.
Turkey was expected to issue a $250 million five-year Eurobond around mid-April, but the government postponed the deal, citing volatility in the U.S. Treasury market.
